title: Propagation of symmetric real stresses and forced cross-polytope subcomplexes in centrally symmetric simplicial complexes
author: Novik, Isabella; Zheng, Hailun
work: The stresses on centrally symmetric complexes and the lower bound theorems
source_version: Algebraic Combinatorics 4 (2021), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/alco.168; exact archived official publisher native/PDF
difficulty_reason: The proof builds a new auxiliary stress by multiplying a mixed derivative by a difference of antipodal sums, then uses its forced symmetry to reconstruct all higher stresses in antipodal variables and force full cross-polytope support. After ordinary differentiation and stress definitions, that construction and the support-propagation argument remain substantive obligations beyond standard qualification-exam calculations. The later face-number corollaries and their named representation theorems do not raise the rating.
source_scope_note: Prove exactly Theorem3.5: on a centrally symmetric simplicial complex over the reals, the printed antisymmetric-or-total-sum linear forms and symmetry of every degree i>1 stress imply symmetry in every degree j>=i; any nonzero stress of degree j>i forces a j-cross-polytope boundary subcomplex. Four source-local lemmas and the full auxiliary differential stress construction are retained. Cohen--Macaulay face-number equality consequences remain uncounted author context. Ordinary polynomial differentiation, free involutions, squarefree support and real polynomial/inverse-system notation are explicit foundations. Lee stress-space and Stanley lower-bound representation results are retained as precise named context but are not assumptions replacing the selected theorem's new differential and support core. Every active original proof, formula, index, macro argument, comment and percent guard in the full author body is retained byte-exact. No diagrams, essential core or mathematical repairs are introduced. Source term affinely independent points in the unselected cross-polytope background is retained without reinterpretation.
